# Frame extension over an occupied floor — the method package

## The situation

You are the construction engineer for a three-lift reinforced concrete frame
extension built over a building whose ground floor stays in use throughout. The
design is fixed and is in the corpus: the storey elevations, the column grid and
sections, the slab thickness and the zone breakdown. **How it gets built is
not.** The construction sequence and the temporary works that make each stage of
it stand up and be reachable are yours, and they are what you issue.

Read `handover/instruction_to_engineer.md` first. It says what the package is
and what the corpus holds.

The rest is the project's own record set: the architect's IFC exports and the
design model schedules taken off them, the issued activity list with its
durations, crane hours and logic, the zone work schedule with the quantities,
the site plan data — the crane chart, the standing positions, the overhead
services, the parts of the building still occupied — the shoring and scaffold
catalogues with their capacities and costs, and the rules: the site's temporary
works procedure TWP-09 with its parameter schedule, and the five public criteria
it adopts.

The limits you have to work to — how much load a shore post may carry, how wide
a platform must be, when a scaffold has to be tied and where, how high a
guardrail sits, when forms may be struck and what that costs you in reshoring,
how many crane hours there are in a shift, what the yard holds, how many gangs
there are, and when the job has to be finished — **are all written down in that
corpus and none of them are restated here.** Finding the governing clause,
reading it and working to it is part of the job, and it is measured (see *The
constraint register*).

## What to deliver

Write these six files into the output directory (`output/`), not into the input
tree. CSV headers are matched case- and punctuation-insensitively; the columns
below are required, and extra columns you find useful are ignored rather than
penalised.

| File | Required columns |
|---|---|
| `construction_sequence.csv` | `activity_id`, `zone`, `level`, `activity_type`, `predecessors`, `duration_days`, `start_day`, `finish_day`, `crew`, `crane_hours`, `workspace_volume_cf` |
| `stability_check.csv` | `stage_id`, `zone`, `level`, `lateral_system`, `demand_lb`, `capacity_lb`, `verdict` |
| `occupancy_report.csv` | `zone_lift`, `zone`, `level`, `occupied_from_day`, `occupied_to_day`, `shored_from_day`, `shored_to_day`, `crane_hours_total`, `laydown_units` |
| `temporary_works.json` | see below |
| `constraint_register.csv` | `requirement`, `document`, `clause`, `value`, `unit`, `items_bound` |
| `method_note.md` | prose, at least **200 words** |

Cover **every zone-lift in the zone work schedule**, and carry **every activity
in the issued activity list** — one row each, keeping the issued `activity_id`.
`duration_days` must be the issued duration and `finish_day` must equal
`start_day + duration_days`; days are whole numbers counted from day 0.

**Work you leave out of the programme is still charged against the site-wide
limits.** There is one crane, one yard, one laydown and one completion date, and
they are drawn on by every zone-lift on the site. An activity that is not in
`construction_sequence.csv` has no day for the verifier to place it on, so it is
charged at the **busiest day you do declare**: its crane hours over its issued
duration, and — for any zone-lift whose activities are not all programmed — its
shored area, its scaffold face, its laydown units and a gang, with the programme
unable to finish before the earliest day the issued logic allows that work to
finish. A zone-lift with no dates is also treated as occupying its zone. Omitting
work does not buy yard stock or crane hours; it costs them.

`stability_check.csv` carries **one row per zone-lift** and is keyed by its
`level` and `zone` columns. `lateral_system` is `temporary_bracing` or
`adjacent_diaphragm`, compared case- and punctuation-insensitively, and
`verdict` is `pass` where the check is satisfied. Any other value is not
recognised.

`occupancy_report.csv` carries **one row per zone-lift**. Its days and totals
are checked against the programme you yourself declared, so a report that does
not agree with your own sequence is a false statement about the site.

`workspace_volume_cf` is the volume the activity occupies: for a scaffold
erection or strike, the zone's face length times the scaffold's base width times
its height above grade; for everything else, the zone's plan area times the
clear height of the lift.

### The tolerances the verifier applies

Several checks compare a number you declare against the same number recomputed
from the corpus. Every tolerance the verifier uses is listed here, because a
threshold you cannot see is one you cannot aim at.

| what is compared | tolerance |
|---|---|
| `shoring.design_load_per_post_lb` against the zone's design load times the square of your grid | 2 percent |
| `stability_check.csv` `demand_lb` against the recomputed lateral demand | 5 percent |
| `scaffold.maximum_intended_load_lb` against the duty class's load | exact |
| `workspace_volume_cf` against the geometry | 5 percent |
| `occupancy_report.csv` `crane_hours_total` against the sum of the issued crane hours | 0.02 hours |
| `occupancy_report.csv` day columns and `laydown_units` | exact |
| `scaffold.platform_capacity_lb`, `crane.rated_capacity_lb` | exact / 2 percent respectively |
| `crane.radius_ft` against the distance from the standing position to the zone centroid | 2 ft |
| `scaffold.height_ft` against the level's height above grade | 0.51 ft |
| `scaffold.height_to_base_ratio` | 0.05 |
| each entry of `scaffold.tie_levels_ft` against the horizontal member the clause puts it at | half a frame lift |
| `duration_days` against the issued duration, and `finish_day − start_day` | exact |

Anything not in this table is a threshold you will find in a shipped document,
not one this note withholds.

### `temporary_works.json`

A single JSON object with `designer`, `drawing_reference` and `zone_lifts`.
`zone_lifts` maps each zone-lift id to an object with `shoring`, `reshore`,
`scaffold`, `bracing` and `crane`. Keys are matched case- and
punctuation-insensitively. The fields the verifier reads:

* `shoring`: `post_type`, `spacing_ft`, `posts`, `design_load_per_post_lb`
* `reshore`: `required` (`yes` / `no`), `posts`, `install_day`, `remove_day`
* `scaffold`: `system`, `base_width_ft`, `bays`, `frame_lifts`, `frames`,
  `planks_per_bay`, `platform_width_in`, `platform_capacity_lb`,
  `platform_levels`, `planks`,
  `guardrail_height_in`, `guardrails`, `height_ft`, `height_to_base_ratio`,
  `tie_levels_ft` (a list of elevations in feet), `tie_columns`, `ties`,
  `maximum_intended_load_lb`, `front_edge_gap_in`, `front_edge_guardrail`,
  `mudsill`, `bearing_pressure_psf`, `access_means`, `fall_protection`
* `bracing`: `lateral_system`, `braced_bays`, `capacity_lb`. `braced_bays`
  must be a whole number greater than or equal to zero for every lateral system;
  use `0` when `lateral_system` is `adjacent_diaphragm`.
* `crane`: `position`, `radius_ft`, `rated_capacity_lb`,
  `encroachment_option` (`option1` / `option2` / `option3`), `min_approach_ft`,
  `demarcated_radius_ft`

`access_means` is one of `stair_tower`, `hook_on_ladder`, `attachable_ladder`,
`stairway_type_ladder`, `portable_ladder`, `integral_access_frame`.
`fall_protection` is one of `guardrail`, `personal_fall_arrest`, `both`.
Anything else is not recognised.

## How your package is checked

Your programme is **re-simulated**, not compared with a key. Your own start and
finish days are replayed against a pristine copy of the site model and every
demand is recomputed from the rows you wrote: each issued dependency, the
strength-gain age your own striking method demands, the crane hours drawn on
each day, the soffit area and scaffold face standing in the yard on each day,
the gangs at work, the laydown, the zones occupied and the stair cores shored.
A programme in a different order is not wrong. A programme whose occupancy
report or whose declared loads do not agree with the programme it declares is.

The temporary-works design is checked the same way: every capacity, width,
ratio, tie interval, clearance and bearing pressure is recomputed from the
shipped catalogues and the shipped clauses against the numbers you declared. A
heavier design than the cheapest one is not wrong; it costs more.

## The constraint register

`constraint_register.csv` is where you record the requirements you actually
applied: one row per requirement, naming the document and the clause it comes
from, its value and unit where it has one, and what it binds. It is scored, and
two floors are stated here because a threshold you cannot see is one you cannot
aim at:

- **register recall floor 0.55** — at least 0.55 of the requirements the grader
  indexes must be present in your register;
- **value-agreement floor 0.40** — at least 0.40 of them must additionally carry
  the right value.

Filing *more* genuine requirements than the grader happens to index is neutral:
thoroughness is not punished. What counts against you is a row that should not
have been filed at all — a citation to a document that is not in force, to a
scope that is not in this package, or to a clause that does not exist.

A requirement the grader holds to be **hard** and which is missing from your
register fails the register family of every zone-lift it binds, which is one of
that zone-lift's hard families (see *What is scored*).

## The method note

`method_note.md` is prose and it is read for four things: which document
governs where the issued set disagrees with itself, the striking and reshoring
method you adopted, the constraint that governs each zone, and the margins you
applied. At least 200 words.

## What is scored

Your score is the mean over the **held-out zone-lifts**, which you cannot query.
Each is checked against thirty constraint families, fifteen of them hard: fourteen
engineering families and the register family, which a zone-lift passes only if
every hard requirement that binds it is registered. A zone-lift scores
0.4 × p + 0.6 × [h = 1] × O, where p is the fraction of the thirty families it
satisfies, h the fraction of the fifteen hard families it satisfies ([h = 1] is 1 when
it satisfies all fifteen, else 0), and O the certified bound divided by the price of
the zone-lift — its temporary works plus the programme cost of the day it finishes — at
most 1. A hard miss removes O. Four of the hard families are **shared across the whole
package**: there is one crane, one yard stock, one set of workspaces and one completion
date, so a programme that spends more of any of them than it needs to spends it out of
every other zone-lift, including the ones you are scored on.

## Attribution

The building in this corpus — its storey elevations, its column grid and
sections, its slab thickness and its stair cores — is derived from:

> LivingBIM Dataset: As-designed and As-built Dataset for an Academic Building
> including BIM 3d models, Point Clouds, and Panoramic Images.
> DOI 10.5281/zenodo.17934615. Licensed **CC BY 4.0**.

Carry that attribution and the CC BY 4.0 conditions with anything you reproduce
from the design schedules.


## Packaging your deliverable

Write the deliverable files named above into `output/`, exactly as the brief describes
them. Then package them into a single zip at `output/submission.zip` — that archive is
what gets graded, and nothing outside it is read.

    cd output && zip -r submission.zip <the deliverable files>

Zip the files themselves; a leading `output/` directory inside the archive is tolerated.
Re-make the zip every time you change a deliverable — a stale `submission.zip` is graded
in preference to the newer loose files beside it, because the loose files are not read.

## Verifier access (blind variant)

No verifier, oracle, or evaluation data of any kind is available in this workspace — the
only checks you can run are the ones you build yourself. Work from the brief and the
documents alone and submit your best final deliverable; it will be graded offline by the
frozen verifier on held-out instances.

# TWP-09 — Temporary works procedure, revision C

**Issued.** This revision supersedes revision B, which is retained in the
document set marked SUPERSEDED and is not in force. Where the two disagree,
revision C governs.

Project: the 3-lift frame extension over the occupied ground floor.
Adopted documents, in force on this project:

* 29 CFR 1926.451, *Scaffolds — General requirements*
* 29 CFR 1926.703, *Requirements for cast-in-place concrete*
* 29 CFR 1926.250, *General requirements for storage*
* 29 CFR 1926.34, *Means of egress*
* 29 CFR 1926.1408, *Power line safety (up to 350 kV) — equipment operations*

## 1. Scope and the method package

1.1 The design is fixed. The construction sequence and the temporary works that
make each stage of it stand up and be reachable are the contractor's, and are
issued as the method package.

1.2 The method package is: the construction sequence, the temporary-works
design, the stability check sheet, the workspace and resource occupancy report,
the constraint register and the method note. A package missing any of these is
not issued.

1.3 The work is divided into zone-lifts. A zone-lift is one zone of one level:
its columns, its slab and the temporary works that carry and reach them.

## 2. Definitions

2.1 *Zone-lift.* One zone of one level. Its activities are `COL` (erect and
grout the precast columns of the lift below the level), `SCAF` (erect the
perimeter access scaffold), `SHOR` (erect the shoring and slab formwork),
`RBAR` (fix the slab reinforcement), `POUR` (place and finish the slab),
`STRK` (strike the slab formwork and shoring) and `SCST` (strike the scaffold).

2.2 *Maximum intended load.* The total load of all persons, equipment, tools,
materials, transmitted loads and other loads reasonably anticipated to be
applied to a scaffold or scaffold component at any one time, as 29 CFR 1926.450
defines it. The duty classes and their loads are in
`catalogue/scaffold_duty_classes.csv`.

2.3 *Early-strike age.* The age in `catalogue/concrete_mix_schedule.csv` at
which the mix may carry its own weight under reshoring. *Full-strength age* is
28 days.

2.4 *Yard stock.* What the site compound holds at any one time. It is measured
in soffit area and in scaffold face, not in components, so the shoring grid a
zone is designed to does not change what the yard can hold.

## 3. The construction sequence

3.1 Every activity shall follow every activity it depends on. The dependencies
are issued in `programme/activity_list.csv` and are not negotiable; a solver may
add dependencies of its own but may not drop one.

3.2 Durations are issued with the activity list and are the durations to be
programmed. `start_day` is the first working day of the activity and
`finish_day` the day after its last, so an activity of 3 days
starting on day 10 finishes on day 13.

3.3 The whole programme shall be complete by day
**250** measured from the first working day of the first
activity. That is the contract completion date and it is one date for the whole
package.

## 4. Access — scaffolds

4.1 Every scaffold shall be capable of supporting, without failure, its own
weight and at least **4 times** the maximum intended load applied or transmitted
to it, as 29 CFR 1926.451(a)(1) requires. The platform shall be planked with
enough `PL-95` units for the plank capacity in
`catalogue/scaffold_components.csv` to meet that requirement.

4.2 Each scaffold platform and walkway shall be at least **18 inches** wide,
29 CFR 1926.451(b)(2).

4.3 The front edge of a platform shall be no more than **14 inches** from the
face of the work unless a guardrail system is erected along the front edge,
29 CFR 1926.451(b)(3).

4.4 A scaffold with a height to base width ratio of more than **four to one**
shall be restrained from tipping by guying, tying or bracing, at the intervals
29 CFR 1926.451(c)(1)(ii) sets: at the closest horizontal member to the 4:1
height, repeated every 20 feet for scaffolds 3 feet wide or less and every
26 feet for scaffolds wider than 3 feet, with the top tie no further than the
4:1 height from the top, at each end and at horizontal intervals not exceeding
30 feet.

4.5 Supported scaffold legs shall bear on base plates and mud sills or other
adequate firm foundation, 29 CFR 1926.451(c)(2). The ground bearing pressure
under a mud sill shall not exceed **2000 pounds per
square foot**.

4.6 A means of access shall be provided where the platform is more than 2 feet
above or below the point of access, 29 CFR 1926.451(e)(1), and a scaffold more
than 35 feet high shall have rest platforms at 35-foot maximum vertical
intervals, 29 CFR 1926.451(e)(2)(iii).

4.7 Each employee on a scaffold more than **10 feet** above a lower level shall
be protected from falling, 29 CFR 1926.451(g)(1). Where that protection is a
guardrail system, the top edge height of the toprail shall be between
**38 inches and 45 inches** above the platform surface,
29 CFR 1926.451(g)(4)(ii). Guardrail systems shall be installed along all open
sides and ends of every platform level, 29 CFR 1926.451(g)(4)(i).

4.8 `PL-95` planks are 10 feet long. On a system whose bay is shorter than the
plank, each plank is laid across its own bay and overlaps its neighbours over
the bearers, 29 CFR 1926.451(b)(7); the planks at each end of a run then extend
beyond the end bearer, and 29 CFR 1926.451(b)(4) and (b)(5)(i) govern those
ends.

## 5. The scaffold duty and the work it serves

5.1 The duty class of the scaffold serving a zone-lift follows from the work it
serves, as clauses 5.3 and 5.4 set out; a scaffold to which neither clause
applies is light duty. The maximum intended load per bay of each class is in
`catalogue/scaffold_duty_classes.csv`.

5.2 A bay is one frame spacing along the face. The number of bays is the zone's
face length divided by the system's bay length, rounded up.

5.3 The concrete pump stands west of the building and reaches bands A to D.
Bands E to G are placed by crane and bucket, which lands at the slab edge, and
the scaffold serving them is heavy duty.

5.4 Where the space below a zone-lift is in continued occupation
(`site/existing_occupation.csv`) the shoring shall carry a protective deck and
the scaffold is medium duty.

## 6. Falsework, shoring and reshoring

6.1 Formwork shall be designed, fabricated, erected, supported, braced and
maintained so that it will carry without failure all vertical and lateral loads
reasonably anticipated, 29 CFR 1926.703(a)(1). The design load per shore post is
the zone's shoring design load times the square of the shore spacing, and it
shall not exceed the post's rated capacity in `catalogue/shoring_catalogue.csv`.
The post's maximum extension shall not be less than the zone's required
extension.

The zone's shoring design load is the slab's self-weight in
`model/slab_schedule.csv`, plus **10 pounds per square foot** for the
formwork, plus a construction live load of **50 pounds per square foot** where
the slab is placed by pump or **75 pounds per square foot** where it is placed
by crane and bucket (clause 5.3), plus **15 pounds per square foot** for the
protective deck where clause 5.4 applies. The zone's required extension is the
height from the lift base to the soffit of the slab being formed
(`model/storey_schedule.csv`), less the **0.75 foot** depth of the form
assembly.

6.2 The lateral system of a partly complete frame shall resist the greater of
the construction wind pressure of **12 pounds per square foot** on
the exposed area and **2 percent** of the vertical load
supported. The vertical load supported by a zone-lift is its shoring design
load (clause 6.1) times its area. It shall be either temporary cross-bracing to `XB-1` in
`catalogue/scaffold_components.csv`, or the completed slab diaphragm of an
adjacent zone at the same level where that slab has reached its early-strike age
before the zone's shoring goes up.

6.3 **Striking.** Forms and shores shall not be removed until the concrete has
gained sufficient strength to carry its weight and the superimposed loads,
29 CFR 1926.703(e)(1). This procedure stipulates the conditions under
(e)(1)(i): the forms and shores of a slab may be struck at the mix's
early-strike age **only where the slab is reshored as the original shores are
removed**, 29 CFR 1926.703(b)(10); otherwise they shall remain in place until
the slab has reached its full-strength age of 28 days.

6.4 Reshoring shall be to `RS-16` at **8 feet** centres
in both directions, and shall not be removed until the slab it supports has
reached its full-strength age, 29 CFR 1926.703(e)(2).

6.5 Drawings for the formwork, the shoring and the scaffolds, including all
revisions, shall be available at the jobsite, 29 CFR 1926.703(a)(2), and the
scaffolds shall be designed by a qualified person, 29 CFR 1926.451(a)(6). The
method package's temporary-works design is that record and it shall name the
qualified designer.

## 7. Workspace

7.1 The workspace an activity needs is the volume of its zone plus the volume
its temporary works occupy: the shoring below the soffit, the scaffold on the
face and the material staged for it.

7.2 **One zone-lift at a time in a zone.** No two zone-lifts of the same zone
may be in progress at the same time. The scaffold on a zone's face and the
shoring under its soffit occupy the same volume at every level, so the level
above cannot start in a zone until the level below has finished in it.

7.3 Two means of egress shall be kept open on every level at all times,
29 CFR 1926.34(a) and (c). Three zones carry a stair core and no more than
**1** of them may be shored on any one day.

## 8. Site resources

8.1 There is **one** tower crane and it works **10 crane
hours** in a shift. An activity's crane hours are issued with the activity list
and are drawn evenly across its duration; the crane hours drawn on any one day
by the whole programme shall not exceed that shift.

8.2 The contractor has **8** gangs. No more than that many activities
may be in progress on any one day.

8.3 The yard holds shoring for **3600 square feet** of soffit
and **120 feet** of scaffold face at any one time. A zone's
shoring occupies the yard from the day its shoring goes up to the day it is
struck; where the slab is reshored, the reshoring occupies
**25 percent** of the zone's area until the slab reaches its
full-strength age. A zone has to be struck before the next can be shored.

8.4 The laydown area holds **16** units of staged material
(`programme/zone_work_schedule.csv`), from the day a zone's shoring goes up to
the day its slab is placed. Material stored on a floor shall not exceed the
maximum safe load limit of that floor, 29 CFR 1926.250(a)(2)(i), and shall not
be placed within 6 feet of a floor opening, 29 CFR 1926.250(b)(1).

## 9. The crane and the overhead line

9.1 The heaviest pick in a zone is issued in `programme/zone_work_schedule.csv`.
The crane's rated capacity at the radius from the standing position to the zone
(`site/crane_chart.csv`, interpolated linearly between chart radii) shall not be
less than it, and the radius shall not exceed the position's maximum working
radius.

9.2 An overhead distribution line runs along the north site boundary at
**34.5 kV** and is not insulated. Because the crane operated up to
its maximum working radius could come closer than **20 feet** to that line,
29 CFR 1926.1408(a)(2) requires Option (1), Option (2) or Option (3). Option (3)
is adopted: the minimum approach distance of Table A shall be determined for the
line's voltage and the work zone shall be demarcated so that no part of the
equipment, load line or load can get closer than it. The demarcated radius shall
be at least the radius the zone needs and no more than the standing position's
distance to the line less the Table A minimum approach.

## 10. Pricing

10.1 A temporary-works item is priced at the cost units of its components in
`catalogue/shoring_catalogue.csv` and `catalogue/scaffold_components.csv`, and
a guardrail bay at 1 unit. A guardrail bay is one bay length of guardrail along
an open side of a platform level, or the guardrail across one end of a
platform level.

10.2 A zone-lift is priced at its temporary-works cost plus
**4 units** for every day from the first working
day of the programme to the day its last activity finishes.

10.3 The method package is judged on the price of each zone-lift against a
certified bound and on whether it satisfies every requirement of this procedure
and of the documents it adopts.

(4) Bagged materials shall be stacked by stepping back the layers and cross-keying the bags at least every 10 bags high.
(5) Materials shall not be stored on scaffolds or runways in excess of supplies needed for immediate operations.
(6) Brick stacks shall not be more than 7 feet in height. When a loose brick stack reaches a height of 4 feet, it shall be tapered back 2 inches in every foot of height above the 4-foot level.

(8) Lumber:
(i) Used lumber shall have all nails withdrawn before stacking.
(ii) Lumber shall be stacked on level and solidly supported sills.
(iii) Lumber shall be so stacked as to be stable and self-supporting.
(iv) Lumber piles shall not exceed 20 feet in height provided that lumber to be handled manually shall not be stacked more than 16 feet high.

(3) Handholds, or other effective means, shall be provided on portable dockboards to permit safe handling.
(4) Positive protection shall be provided to prevent railroad cars from being moved while dockboards or bridge plates are in position.

General requirements.

lifts, the criteria for which are set out

paragraphs (a)(2), (a)(3), (a)(4), (a)(5)

own weight and at least 4 times the

transmitted to it.

capable of supporting, without failure,
at least 6 times the maximum intended
load applied or transmitted to that
rope.
(4) Each suspension rope, including
connecting hardware, used on adjustable suspension scaffolds shall be capable of supporting, without failure, at
least 6 times the maximum intended
load applied or transmitted to that
rope with the scaffold operating at either the rated load of the hoist, or 2
(minimum) times the stall load of the
hoist, whichever is greater.

(5) The stall load of any scaffold hoist
shall not exceed 3 times its rated load.
(6) Scaffolds shall be designed by a
qualified person and shall be constructed and loaded in accordance with
that design. Non-mandatory appendix
A to this subpart contains examples of
criteria that will enable an employer
to comply with paragraph (a) of this
section.

decked between the front uprights and
the guardrail supports as follows:

plank, fabricated plank, fabricated
deck, or fabricated platform) shall be
installed so that the space between adjacent units and the space between the
platform and the uprights is no more
than 1 inch (2.5 cm) wide, except where
the employer can demonstrate that a
wider space is necessary (for example,
to fit around uprights when side brackets are used to extend the width of the
platform).
(ii) Where the employer makes the
demonstration provided for in paragraph (b)(1)(i) of this section, the platform shall be planked or decked as
fully as possible and the remaining
open space between the platform and
the uprights shall not exceed 91⁄2 inches
(24.1 cm).
Exception to paragraph (b)(1): The requirement in paragraph (b)(1) to provide full planking or decking does not
apply to platforms used solely as walkways or solely by employees performing scaffold erection or dismantling. In these situations, only the
planking that the employer establishes
is necessary to provide safe working
conditions is required.
(2) Except as provided in paragraphs
(b)(2)(i) and (b)(2)(ii) of this section,
each scaffold platform and walkway
shall be at least 18 inches (46 cm) wide.
(i) Each ladder jack scaffold, top
plate bracket scaffold, roof bracket
scaffold, and pump jack scaffold shall
be at least 12 inches (30 cm) wide.
There is no minimum width requirement for boatswains’ chairs.
NOTE TO PARAGRAPH (b)(2)(i): Pursuant to
an administrative stay effective November
29, 1996 and published in the FEDERAL REGISTER on November 25, 1996, the requirement

in paragraph (b)(2)(i) that roof bracket scaffolds be at least 12 inches wide is stayed
until November 25, 1997 or until rulemaking
regarding the minimum width of roof bracket scaffolds has been completed, whichever is
later.

(ii) Where scaffolds must be used in
areas that the employer can demonstrate are so narrow that platforms
and walkways cannot be at least 18
inches (46 cm) wide, such platforms and
walkways shall be as wide as feasible,

walkways shall be protected from fall
hazards by the use of guardrails and/or

(3) Except as provided in paragraphs
(b)(3) (i) and (ii) of this section, the
front edge of all platforms shall not be
more than 14 inches (36 cm) from the
face of the work, unless guardrail systems are erected along the front edge
and/or personal fall arrest systems are
used in accordance with paragraph (g)
of this section to protect employees
from falling.
(i) The maximum distance from the
face for outrigger scaffolds shall be 3
inches (8 cm);

face for plastering and lathing operations shall be 18 inches (46 cm).

at least 6 inches (15 cm).

support more than 12 inches (30 cm) unless the platform is designed and installed so that the cantilevered portion
of the platform is able to support employees and/or materials without tipping, or has guardrails which block employee access to the cantilevered end.
(ii) Each platform greater than 10

support more than 18 inches (46 cm),

cantilevered end.

§ 1926.703 Requirements for cast-in-place concrete.
(a) General requirements for formwork. (1) Formwork shall be designed, fabricated, erected, supported, braced and maintained so that it will be capable of supporting without failure all vertical and lateral loads that may reasonably be anticipated to be applied to the formwork. Formwork which is designed, fabricated, erected, supported, braced and maintained in conformance with the appendix to this section will be deemed to meet the requirements of this paragraph.
(2) Drawings or plans, including all revisions, for the jack layout, formwork (including shoring equipment), working decks, and scaffolds, shall be available at the jobsite.
(b) Shoring and reshoring. (1) All shoring equipment (including equipment used in reshoring operations) shall be inspected prior to erection to determine that the equipment meets the requirements specified in the formwork drawings.
(2) Shoring equipment found to be damaged such that its strength is reduced to less than that required by § 1926.703(a)(1) shall not be used for shoring.
(3) Erected shoring equipment shall be inspected immediately prior to, during, and immediately after concrete placement.
(4) Shoring equipment that is found to be damaged or weakened after erection, such that its strength is reduced to less than that required by § 1926.703(a)(1), shall be immediately reinforced.
(5) The sills for shoring shall be sound, rigid, and capable of carrying the maximum intended load.
(6) All base plates, shore heads, extension devices, and adjustment screws shall be in firm contact, and secured when necessary, with the foundation and the form.
(7) Eccentric loads on shore heads and similar members shall be prohibited unless these members have been designed for such loading.
(8) Whenever single post shores are used one on top of another (tiered), the employer shall comply with the following specific requirements in addition to the general requirements for formwork:
(i) The design of the shoring shall be prepared by a qualified designer and the erected shoring shall be inspected by an engineer qualified in structural design.
(ii) The single post shores shall be vertically aligned.
(iii) The single post shores shall be spliced to prevent misalignment.
(iv) The single post shores shall be adequately braced in two mutually perpendicular directions at the splice level. Each tier shall also be diagonally braced in the same two directions.
(9) Adjustment of single post shores to raise formwork shall not be made after the placement of concrete.
(10) Reshoring shall be erected, as the original forms and shores are removed, whenever the concrete is required to support loads in excess of its capacity.
(c) Vertical slip forms. (1) The steel rods or pipes on which jacks climb or by which the forms are lifted shall be—
(i) Specifically designed for that purpose; and
(ii) Adequately braced where not encased in concrete.
(2) Forms shall be designed to prevent excessive distortion of the structure during the jacking operation.
(3) All vertical slip forms shall be provided with scaffolds or work platforms where employees are required to work or pass.
